title: Vṛndāvana: seven temples
summary: A devotional walk through the seven temple tradition, from Madana-mohana to Śyāmasundara.
body:
This route follows the seven temples remembered together in Vraja's worship tradition. It begins at Madana-mohana, crosses to Govindadeva, then turns through Rādhā-Dāmodara and the Keshī-ghāṭa shrines before finishing at Śyāmasundara in the heart of Vṛndāvana.

All seven stops are located on the map. Distances are straight-line estimates between them, not measured walking paths through the lanes.

stops.note: Begin with the Deity who Captures even the mind of Cupid.
Cross east to the great temple of Kṛṣṇa as protector of the cows.
Near the Yamunā, remembered for closeness and intimate service.
A small, intimate shrine of Rādhā's loving service.
The temple that keeps the household mood of Nanda's Vraja.
A historic shrine of the gopīs' beloved Deity.
Finish with the dark-hued beloved of Rādhā in Vṛndāvana's centre.

title: Govardhana half-day
summary: A mapped half-day sample of Govardhana parikrama, from Jatipura to Mānasī Gaṅgā.
body:
This half-day walk samples the Govardhana parikrama from Jatipura on the hill's western side to Mānasī Gaṅgā on the eastern side. It passes Govinda-kuṇḍa and Surabhi-kuṇḍa, turns through Aaniyor and Dāna-ghāṭī, and ends at the Harideva and Mānasī Devī shrines.

Every stop is in the Govardhana area, not in Vṛndāvana town. Distances are straight-line estimates between located stops; the roads and lanes of the actual parikrama will usually be longer.

stops.note: Begin at Jatipura, the western village approach to the sacred hill.
A kunda on the Govardhana side, associated with Kṛṣṇa's cowherd pastimes.
Surabhi-kuṇḍa keeps the memory of the wish-fulfilling cow in Vraja.
Aaniyor is remembered in Vraja tradition for Śrī Śrīnātha.
Dāna-ghāṭī recalls the giving and bargaining of Kṛṣṇa's dāna-līlā.
Śrī Harideva is traditionally honoured beside Mānasī-gaṅgā.
Finish at Mānasī Devī, the Devī form traditionally installed at Govardhana.

title: Rādhā-kuṇḍa circuit
summary: A mapped loop around the lakes, groves and āśramas of the Rādhā-kuṇḍa area.
body:
This circuit uses the places around Rādhā-kuṇḍa. It moves through Nārada-kuṇḍa and Uddhava-kuṇḍa, passes Gvāla-pokharā and Mukharavinda, and turns through Cakaleśvara before reaching a quiet āśrama stop.

The kundas themselves remain central to meditation here. Distances are straight-line estimates between the located stops.

stops.note: Begin at Nārada-kuṇḍa, named for the sage's remembered presence.
Uddhava-kuṇḍa recalls the messenger who brought Kṛṣṇa's words to Vraja.
A cowherd pond on the quiet approach to the groves.
Mukharavinda keeps the memory of Kṛṣṇa's lotus-like face in Vraja.
Cakaleśvara Mahādeva marks the Śiva presence guarding this sector.
Finish at a modern āśrama of bhajana in the Rādhā-kuṇḍa area.
